answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a refundable stake locked for a fixed window, like a sable-dark deposit that only returns after honest work. Every payment then carries a verifiable thread linking the agent's past transactions, so a flood of fresh identities has no history to borrow. Peers mirror each other's records: if the same stake or thread appears under two names, both are slashed. Creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive, because each one needs its own locked deposit and its own clean, checkable history.
